subject: convoyHauler
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: armoured convoy hauler guarding a sealed cargo pod.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm planning a six-wheeled armoured hauler truck design with a cab, armour plating, a turret, and a sealed cargo pod featuring glowing seals, neon strips, an antenna, and decal details. Since it's a static vehicle, I can skip joints or just keep them minimal for the wheels.

Now I'm working out the joint hierarchy with a chassis root and wheel/turret joints, sizing the body at roughly 9m long, 3m wide, and 3.4m tall with the cab facing forward and the pod at the rear. I'm placing six wheels across three axles using cylinder geometry for tires and smaller glowing hubs, then building the chassis frame as boxes with panelled armour textures imported from a kit, keeping colors within the limit before starting on the cab's frustum shape.

Writing cab extrusion profile...

Adding a windshield texture, then shaping the front bumper as a ram plow via extrusion with hazard stripe graphics, plus amber/cyan headlight glows and magenta/cyan neon side strips, and panelled armor skirts along the chassis.

Now I'm lathing a cylindrical cargo pod along the z-axis, defining a tapered profile that forms a capsule shape sitting above the bed, and thinking through how to cradle it onto the chassis.

Adding glow rings and a hatch...

For side decals I'll embed a thin box decal at x=±1.25 spanning 1.19–1.31 so the texture shows cleanly on the outer face without floating or clipping, using opaque SVG panels and white backing. For the rear, I'm adding a turret ahead of the pod on the rear frame—cylinder base, box body, twin forward barrels, and a glow sensor.

I'm reworking the layout so the cab spans z 1.0–4.3 and the pod shifts to z -4.3–0.7 to avoid overlap, moving the turret onto the cab roof at z=1.9, y=3.1 instead of the pod. I'm adjusting the pod's profile curve to a 5.0 length taper with points from the nose to the tail to match the new z-range.

Now I'm adding escort details: a flashing light bar on the cab roof, antennas, mirrors, and exhaust stacks placed outside the pod radius at x±1.45 to clear the cab width of ±1.3. I'm also sketching fender boxes above the wheel positions and reconciling the chassis and wheel widths so the fenders sit correctly over the wheels without clipping the body.

I'm resolving overlap issues by narrowing the cab to ±1.2 and shifting the wheel centers outward to x 1.55 with a width of 0.6 (1.25–1.85), giving a total truck width near 3.9–4.0 meters, which keeps the wheel inner edge just clear of the cab wall while making the vehicle appropriately broad for a heavy truck.

Now I'm placing the chassis frame, deck, and pod cradle: chassis box sits between y 0.75–1.2, wheel radius 0.7 centered at y 0.7 to keep clearance above ground, the bed deck goes on top around y 1.29, and I'm adding three cradle ribs along the deck to seat the cylindrical pod plus tie-down strap rings to secure it in place.

Dark iron rings at radius ~1.3 and height ~0.35 wrap the pod for the straps, with thinner glow rings at radius ~1.32-1.33 offset slightly to either side for a seam-light effect — keeping it simple since exact cylinder segment alignment isn't critical. Now moving on to the rear section.

For the rear I'm adding a bumper box with red glowing tail lights, a rear guard bar and shield, plus angled armor panels on the cab sides and a sensor mast topped with a dish made from a cylinder and cone. I'm also putting thin magenta underglow boxes beneath the chassis near the sides for an emissive edge-light effect, and planning out five decal textures: windshield, hazard stripes, hatch emblem, side logo, and a unit number marking.

I'm now adding a sixth texture for a door plate reading "C-07" plus a front grille decal, defining paint materials for the hull, pod, and accent trim using metal and panelled finishes, and setting up a helper function to quickly generate boxes attached to the chassis bone. I'm also working out the joint hierarchy, with a root bone at the chassis and separate wheel bones positioned at each axle with their rotation direction set along the X axis.

Still building wheel geometry...

Now I'm setting up the turret with a yaw joint on the chassis and a pitch joint for the gun mount above it.

I'm placing the turret and lightbar along the sloped roof, and planning glow effects for non-painted parts. Now I'm settling on the chassis color scheme, using an iron paint base with darker paneling.

Working out the color palette with navy hull, plate accents, and neon cyan, magenta, amber, and hazard yellow highlights. I'm positioning the cab's side door texture planes so their text faces outward correctly regardless of orientation, and now figuring out placement for the front cab face.

Still placing elements...

Positioning headlights narrower than grille width so they don't overlap, then working out windshield slope, roof visor, side window glow planes, and door panel placement on the cab sides.

Now I'm placing the mirrors as rod-and-box arms beside the cab, and working out exhaust stack cylinders mounted on brackets near the wheel pods, making sure they clear the fender and pod radius.

I'm positioning the rear, middle, and front wheels along the z-axis, then adding fender boxes above each wheel pair and sizing fuel tank cylinders to sit between the axles without colliding with the pods or chassis width.

Now I'm sketching rear details for the chassis — a tail section with the deck and pod ending around z=0.7 to -4.3, plus a rear cap, bumper, and taillights to close out the back end.

I'm also laying out small accent features: an amber rear beacon, a roof antenna with a glowing tip, and a two-tone roof lightbar with red and blue glow sections split symmetrically across the center.

Now I'm placing the pod hatch with its textured top plane and support box, positioning side ID logo panels flush against the pod walls, and considering armored ridge strips before deciding they'd interfere with the hatch geometry.

Designing SVG textures for each part: a sealed hatch emblem, a magenta chevron freight logo, hazard stripes, a glowing cyan windshield pattern with scanlines, and horizontal glowing grille slats, plus a door decal with convoy ID text.

Now I'm defining the paint materials—a tarnished iron hull, a mottled dark-teal steel pod, and dark charcoal chassis tones—to give the vehicle a weathered cyberpunk feel before assembling the final code.

I'm setting up the extrusion and lathe helpers for shaping parts, then wiring up joints—chassis root, hinge joints for wheels, and a yaw joint for turret-mounted bones. With that structure clear, I'm ready to write the final build.
